question: Which two features are used to allow a nondisruptive upgrade for the ISSU process? (Choose two.)
theory: A nondisruptive ISSU relies on high-availability mechanisms already built into dual-supervisor NX-OS platforms: Stateful Switchover (SSO) keeps the standby supervisor's control-plane state synchronized with the active supervisor so a switchover during the upgrade doesn't reset protocol state, while Nonstop Forwarding (NSF), Cisco's graceful-restart implementation, lets neighboring routers keep forwarding using cached routes while the local control plane restarts, hiding the brief outage from the rest of the network. Advanced licensing, a connectivity management processor, and stand-alone graceful restart are not themselves the redundancy mechanisms that make ISSU nondisruptive. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — High Availability Foundations for ISSU: SSO and NSF)
